title: Which Specific Level of Open-Plan Office Despair Are You Currently Experiencing?
dek: Your desk is a 'touch-down space' and your sanity is a legacy system. Let's find out exactly how far gone you are.
author: dirk-hotfix

questions.q: A coworker you barely know begins eating a hard-boiled egg three feet from your monitor. Your immediate reaction is:

answers.a: Politely ignore it while calculating the exact air-current velocity carrying the scent toward your face.
Slowly put on noise-canceling headphones, even though they don't block smells.
Stare blankly at a spreadsheet until the egg becomes the only thing in the universe.
Send a passive-aggressive Slack message to the general channel about 'shared space etiquette'.

questions.q: Which of these 'collaboration tools' do you fear the most?

answers.a: The whiteboard that is perpetually covered in a 2019 brainstorming session.
The beanbag chair that is impossible to exit with dignity.
The 'huddle space' where you can be seen by everyone in the building.
The shared calendar that shows you exactly when your boss is 'Focusing'.

questions.q: You have a high-priority call, but the only available spot is next to the industrial printer. You:

answers.a: Try to blend into the beige wallpaper and hope the printer doesn't jam.
Lean into the noise and pretend it's just 'dynamic office energy'.
Begin a conversation with the printer, as it is the only thing that understands you.
Loudly complain about the acoustics to whoever is standing nearest to you.

questions.q: What is your current relationship with your 'Hot Desk'?

answers.a: I have a designated spot, but I'm terrified someone will move my stapler.
I carry my entire life in a nylon tote bag like a corporate nomad.
I often forget which floor I'm on for the first ten minutes of the day.
I spend twenty minutes scouting the room for the desk furthest from the kitchen.

questions.q: Your manager asks for a 'quick sync' in the middle of the open floor. You feel:

answers.a: A slight spike in cortisol, but you maintain a professional smile.
The urge to physically merge with your ergonomic chair.
A strange sense of detachment, as if you are watching this happen to a different person.
An overwhelming desire to accidentally spill a latte on the sync notes.

questions.q: What is the primary sound in your peripheral hearing right now?

answers.a: The distant hum of a ventilation system that isn't actually working.
A coworker explaining a 'pivot' for the fourteenth time today.
The sound of your own internal screaming, muffled by a fleece vest.
The aggressive clicking of a mechanical keyboard from the person next to you.

denial.title: The Optimistic Placeholder
denial.body: You still believe the 'synergy' promised in the onboarding slide deck is real. You keep a small succulent on your desk despite the lack of natural light and you genuinely think a new ergonomic mousepad will solve your burnout. You are currently in the 'acceptance' phase of a disaster that hasn't fully hit you yet. You likely still use the word 'opportunity' when describing a task that takes six hours and pays nothing.
denial.share: I'm The Optimistic Placeholder. I still believe the breakroom fruit is a perk!

coping.title: The High-Functioning Nomad
coping.body: You have mastered the art of the 'invisible shield.' You possess three different types of noise-canceling technology and can navigate a crowded office without making eye contact with a single soul. Your survival depends on a precise routine of caffeine and strategic bathroom breaks. You don't have a desk; you have a series of temporary alliances with various power outlets and a very sturdy backpack.
coping.share: I'm The High-Functioning Nomad. My noise-canceling headphones are my only true friends.

dissociation.title: The Human Screensaver
dissociation.body: You have achieved a state of corporate nirvana where you are physically present but mentally orbiting Jupiter. You can sit through a forty-minute meeting about 'deliverables' while imagining a world where you live in a cabin with no electricity. Your stare is so vacant that coworkers have stopped asking you for things, which is the only reason you're still productive. You are less a person and more a collection of habits in a business-casual shirt.
dissociation.share: I'm The Human Screensaver. I haven't actually perceived a colleague since Tuesday.

hostility.title: The Perimeter Guard
hostility.body: You are one 'quick chat' away from a complete systemic collapse. You track the movements of your colleagues like a hawk monitoring a field of mice, noting exactly who takes the longest lunch and who leaves a tuna sandwich in the fridge. Your emails have shifted from 'Best regards' to 'Regards' to simply 'Sent from my iPhone.' You don't want a promotion; you want a wall—a thick, soundproof, ten-foot wall between you and everyone else.
hostility.share: I'm The Perimeter Guard. I can hear you breathing from three cubicles away and I hate it.
